title: Dragos researchers: canary credentials in about two million test prompts show at least three AI hosting providers compromised
date_note: Date of the Dragos report; the page gives no earlier day for the breaches themselves.
geo_basis: global report; pin is a placeholder for the United States
summary: Dragos says it submitted approximately two million prompts containing canary credentials and saw seeded prompts used in attempts to access its test systems and canary AWS accounts, indicating at least three AI hosting providers were compromised. OpenRouter says it off-boarded three providers, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility and found no breach of OpenRouter itself. BleepingComputer names the three as Together AI, Phala and Novita.
plain: Researchers planted fake credentials in prompts sent to AI services and saw them used, which they say shows at least three AI hosting providers were compromised. OpenRouter removed three providers.
exec: Dragos says its canary credentials in prompts sent to AI services were later used, so data sent in prompts to third-party AI providers may be exposed.
action: OpenRouter says it notified all potentially affected customers; General advice: avoid putting real keys or passwords in prompts and rotate any that were.
impact: Dragos says the largest breach involved a couple hundred of its AWS canary keys. OpenRouter says it off-boarded three providers and removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility.

sources.name: Dragos: Three breaches, endless leaks: Your AI supply chain needs canaries
OpenRouter: data processing incidents on inference providers

validation.note: Dragos (the researchers' own report) and OpenRouter (provider's own announcement, which links the Dragos report) are primary pages; Sekurak and BleepingComputer relay them. BleepingComputer names the three removed providers as Together AI, Phala and Novita.

evidence.quote: we submitted approximately two million prompts containing unique URLs and canary token credentials
The largest breach involved a couple hundred of our AWS keys.
Removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility.

review.note: Compared two million prompts, largest breach, at least three providers, 125 ZDR endpoints, three off-boarded, no OpenRouter breach, notified customers against Dragos, OpenRouter and BleepingComputer
